note: Geography / geo-entertainment hook formulas. Loaded only with --profile geo (hookscore.py, swipe.py), alongside the 21 general formulas in hooks.json, which stay untouched. A geography hook pulls on an ANOMALY - a fact that contradicts the map in the viewer's head - not on loss. The examples show the SHAPE. Any example used in a real script still goes through geo-factcheck like every other claim.
rules: Name the place, or show it on the map in the first 3 seconds. An anomaly nobody can locate is just trivia.
The map is the hook. Write the line for what is ON SCREEN when it is said.
One anomaly per hook. Two strange facts cancel each other out.
Never overstate it. 'Only', 'first', 'largest' and 'nobody' are claims and they get checked.
Explain why it matters to an American viewer in one clause when the place is not in the U.S.

hooks.name: The Only Way In
hooks.shape: A place you can only reach through somewhere it does not belong to.
hooks.example: There is a town in Washington State you can only drive to by going through Canada.
hooks.fails_when: Dies if 'only' is not literally true. Check boat, air and seasonal routes before you say it.

hooks.name: The Place That Shouldn't Exist
hooks.shape: A piece of one place sitting inside another, shown on the map.
hooks.example: This Spanish town is completely surrounded by France - and it has been for centuries.
hooks.fails_when: The map has to make it obvious in one frame. If it needs a legend, use a different formula.

hooks.name: Why Is It Like This?
hooks.shape: Point at a strange line or shape on the map and ask why.
hooks.example: Why does this tiny piece of land north of the border belong to Minnesota?
hooks.fails_when: The answer must be a story, not 'surveying error'. If the why is boring, the video is too.

hooks.name: The Empty Map
hooks.shape: A huge area where almost nobody lives, and the reason is not the obvious one.
hooks.example: Almost nobody lives in this part of America, and it is not because of the desert.
hooks.fails_when: Needs a population figure with a source year. 'Nobody' is rarely literally true - say 'almost'.

hooks.name: The Border That Breaks the Rules
hooks.shape: A border doing something borders are not supposed to do.
hooks.example: In this town the border between two countries runs straight through people's living rooms.
hooks.fails_when: Show it physically - the line on the pavement, the marker, the split building.

hooks.name: The Scale Shock
hooks.shape: A size comparison that breaks the viewer's mental map.
hooks.example: Alaska is bigger than Texas, California and Montana combined.
hooks.fails_when: State which area you compare - total, land, or water - and the source. Map projections lie, so animate true size.

hooks.name: Technically True
hooks.shape: A legal or technical status that sounds wrong.
hooks.example: Technically, this island in the middle of a river belongs to a country you cannot see from it.
hooks.fails_when: The technicality must be documented - a treaty, a court case, a statute. Name it in the body.

hooks.name: The Extreme Place
hooks.shape: People living somewhere at the limit - highest, coldest, most remote.
hooks.example: This is one of the most remote inhabited places on Earth, and people still live there year round.
hooks.fails_when: Superlatives need two independent sources. Prefer 'one of the' unless the record is official.

hooks.name: The Hidden Reason
hooks.shape: Something everyone sees on a map, and the cause nobody guesses.
hooks.example: A string of East Coast cities sits on the same invisible line, and the real reason is where the rivers stop being navigable.
hooks.fails_when: The reason must be sourced to research, not a popular theory. Say 'scientists think' when it is a theory.

hooks.name: The Map Is Lying
hooks.shape: The map in the viewer's head is wrong, and you prove it on screen.
hooks.example: The map you grew up with makes Greenland look as big as Africa. It is not even close.
hooks.fails_when: Show the correction visually inside 10 seconds - a true-size overlay, not a sentence.
